slides.heading: Longest Common Subsequence
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Longest Common Subsequence, a hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: One LCS of two strings as a list of chars.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. One LCS of two strings as a list of chars.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Match characters along two prefixes: a match extends the diagonal, otherwise take the better of dropping one character.
slides.narration: Match characters along two prefixes: a match extends the diagonal, otherwise take the better of dropping one character.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: all subsequences of one string → O(2ⁿ · m)
slides.narration: Enumerating subsequences is exponential. A DP over prefixes is n times m, and backtracking recovers the actual letters.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Equal characters add one to the diagonal
3. Otherwise take the max of top or left
slides.narration: Step by step. First, build the LCS length table. Second, equal characters add one to the diagonal. Third, otherwise take the max of top or left. Fourth, backtrack to recover the letters.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Fill: match → diagonal + 1, else max(up, left)
slides.narration: Fill the table: matching letters take the diagonal plus one; otherwise the max of above and left. Green cells are matches.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Backtrack from the bottom-right
slides.narration: Backtrack from the bottom-right: on a match, take the letter and go diagonally; otherwise move toward the larger neighbour.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: LCS = XYZW
slides.narration: The longest common subsequence is X, Y, Z, W, length 4.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We fill the table with the match-or-max rule, then walk back from n, m, prepending matching characters.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times m. Space is O of n times m.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Ties in backtracking: any choice valid
slides.narration: Mind the padding row and column. Ties during backtracking can go either way.
